From: Emma Thomas <emma.thomas@nimbushealth.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Order form redlines attached — payment & tax flow questions

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — attached is our redlined order form (OrderForm_Nimbus_Redline_v3.docx) and a note from our finance team. High-level asks we need clarified before we can route to legal/exec for signature: 

- Invoicing entity: we need invoices split between Nimbus US and Nimbus EU (billing to different legal entities).
- Net terms: procurement is asking for Net 60; sales proposal shows Net 30.
- Minimum commit: want quarterly true-up rather than annual milestone — they prefer prorated ramp.
- Taxes: they requested Redwood to accept reverse-charge in EU and provide a tax certificate; they may withhold VAT unless we provide evidence.

Can you flag which of these are negotiable and how Redwood would expect invoicing flows to work? If you can share an alternative payment path and a timeline for providing tax evidence that would help speed review.

Attachments: OrderForm_Nimbus_Redline_v3.docx, TaxCert_Nimbus.pdf

Emma Thomas
Senior Procurement Manager
Nimbus Health

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form redlines attached — payment & tax flow questions

Emma — appreciate the clear redlines and the tax note. Quick read and proposed path below, copying legal (Kimberly) and finance (Ben) so they can validate wording.

Summary of Redwood's proposed compromise:
1) Invoicing entities: we can split invoices by jurisdiction. Operationally we’ll invoice Nimbus US for US-usage and Nimbus EU for EU-usage. Each invoice will reference the shared order form and allocation table.
2) Net terms: we can move to Net 45 (midpoint) to bridge Net 30/60. If Nimbus requires Net 60 we’ll need an exec credit approval — please confirm if procurement can accept Net 45 for signature cadence.
3) Minimum commit: we accept quarterly true-ups for the first 12 months (prorated ramp). After 12 months, annual true-ups apply.
4) Taxes: we will provide a Redwood tax annex template and accept EU reverse-charge only if Nimbus provides a VAT registration + signed tax residency annex. If withholding occurs, invoices will reflect gross amounts and the order form will include a clause to allocate withholding responsibility per jurisdiction.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly: please advise on the clean clause language for the tax annex and withholding carve-outs (see attached initial note).
- Ben: confirm whether Finance is comfortable issuing split invoices and whether separate POs are required per legal entity.
- Emma: let us know whether procurement can take Net 45 and the PO timing. If yes, I’ll prepare a final amendment/DocuSign package.

Subject: RE: Order form redlines attached — tax & invoicing approach

Thanks for the ping, Karthik. I reviewed the redline and drafted proposed language that accomplishes two things: (a) enables split invoicing by jurisdiction while keeping a single canonical Order Form; and (b) preserves Redwood’s position on tax/responsibility. See highlights below and attached amendment (RDW-proposed-amendment-20260827.docx).

Key legal notes:
- Invoicing: proposed clause will allow Redwood to issue separate invoices to the entities listed in Schedule A. Each invoice references the Order Form ID and the allocation % per month. This protects us operationally while meeting Nimbus’s procurement requirement.
- Net terms: Net 45 is commercially reasonable; I can draft a sign-off path that lists Net 45 in the Order Form and an optional Net 60 exception section that requires VP-level approval and credit review. This avoids blocking signature while preserving our credit control.
- Withholding & VAT: Redwood will accept reverse-charge treatment in EU only upon receipt of (1) a completed tax residency annex signed by Nimbus; and (2) a validated VAT registration. If Nimbus withholds tax despite evidence, invoices must show gross amounts and Nimbus will be responsible for any related reporting; we add a mutual cooperation clause for refund/reconciliation.

Operational asks for finance (Ben):
- Can Redwood’s billing system generate separate invoices with a shared Order Form ID and allocation lines? If so, what POs/fields do we need on the invoice to ensure AR ties correctly?

If Finance is good, I suggest we send the attached amendment to Nimbus with tracked changes, present Net 45 as the default, and include an annex for tax evidence. Karthik, once you confirm procurement is okay with Net 45 I’ll finalize wording and loop in Lauren for signature authority confirmation.

Emma — following internal review I’m attaching the proposed amendment (RDW-proposed-amendment-20260827.docx) with tracked changes and a summary of the execution path. Thank you for the patience while we routed this.

What Redwood can agree to now:
- Invoicing: split invoices by legal entity as shown in Schedule A; each invoice will reference the same Order Form ID and include allocation lines.
- Net terms: default Net 45 on the Order Form. We can include an exception path to request Net 60 which requires VP-level approval and a short credit review (we can fast-track on receipt of PO + financials).
- Minimum commit: quarterly true-ups for months 1–12 (prorated), then annual true-ups thereafter.
- Taxes: Redwood will accept EU reverse-charge only once Nimbus signs the Tax Residency Annex and provides VAT registration. If withholding occurs incorrectly, parties agree to reconcile and cooperate per the annex.

Docs & execution:
- Attached: RDW-proposed-amendment-20260827.docx (clean + redlines).
- DocuSign package: https://app.docusign.com/embedded/1234abcd (contains Order Form + Amendment + Tax Annex).
- Next step for Nimbus: confirm Net 45 acceptance and provide PO(s) for the invoicing entities. Once we receive PO(s) we’ll send the DocuSign and aim to have countersignature within 48 hours.
